C1.rationale: The unit is almost constraint-free by design: it disclaims prescriptiveness outright and frames every entry as a judgment condition ('Use when') rather than a directive, which is exactly the delegated-judgment shape the post's comment-density rewrite models. Short of 5 only because the 'Extending the glossary' steps carry mild authoring prescription and no entry explains why the model needs the distinction it draws.

evidence.quote: The list is descriptive of current practice, not prescriptive: extend it as the vocabulary matures.
the *Use when* column does the disambiguation

C2.rationale: The unit has no invocation interface — no arguments, flags, or typed options. It is a pure narrative/tabular reference, which the rubric explicitly routes to n/a.

C3.rationale: Everything is inlined into one always-loaded file: six full glossary tables (~50 entries) plus an authoring procedure, with nothing split into a separately-loadable surface. Partial credit only for the boundary that pushes plugin-specific vocabulary out to the plugin's own rules and the See-also/Related pointers; the bulk of the material is exactly the kind that should sit behind a lookup rather than be paid for upfront on every turn.

evidence.quote: | Hoist | Move a declaration to an outer scope so more callers can reach it | Scope of access is the reason for moving |

C4.rationale: The unit is unusually disciplined about ownership: it states an explicit rule for what does NOT belong here, and the Related section names which surface owns the formal definitions it only gestures at. Short of 5 because a few entries ('Adversarial review', 'Spin up a subagent', 'Checkpoint') still carry a second one-line definition of concepts already owned by a named skill or rule.

evidence.quote: If the term is plugin-specific (e.g. blueprint's `ADR`, `PRD`, `PRP`), keep it in that plugin's rules and cross-link instead.
`.claude/rules/agent-development.md` — formal definitions of subagent, worktree isolation, team

C5.rationale: This is the anchor-1 case almost in full: ~7.7KB loaded on every turn of every session, the overwhelming majority of which defines standard software-engineering vocabulary a Claude 5 model already uses correctly unprompted — happy path, edge cases, dry-run, staging, extract/inline, user story, invariants. Nothing here must hold on every turn regardless of what was asked; word choice matters only when writing a commit, PR title, or plan, i.e. it is intent-triggered. The 'Extending the glossary' section is a procedure that matters only when someone edits this one file. A genuinely house-specific residue exists ('Set the seam', 'Park', 'Pick up where we left off') but it is a handful of rows carrying the token cost of fifty.

C6.rationale: Genuinely definitional material with no mechanical, repeatable work described in prose, so the dimension does not bite hard; the unit does point at the real owning artifacts (a named dispatch skill, a sibling rule) where a term's substance is procedural, though those pointers are thin and several terms that ARE backed by an executable skill get a prose one-liner here instead of a reference.

top_finding: Cut the file to the handful of terms that carry house-specific meaning plus the ownership pointers, and move the rest (or the whole glossary) to an on-demand lookup surface, since a Claude 5 model already uses 'happy path', 'dry-run', 'extract', and 'staging' correctly without being told on every turn.
counter_finding: The ownership boundary — plugin-specific vocabulary stays in that plugin's rules and cross-links here, with Related naming agent-development.md as the owner of the formal subagent definitions — is cheap, non-obvious, and prevents exactly the duplication C4 penalises, so it should survive any trim.
